question: do the Evolution bytes of a TrueHD access unit separate the titles Dolby opens from the ones it refuses at the object output
method: oadec emdf --dump 1 on the first access unit that carries a container, comparing the extra-data header, the parities, the Evolution frame and the first ten bytes of the OAMD payload
answer: no. A Quiet Place (refused) and F1 (opened) match in every length and in the protection layout and differ in one byte of the payload, 0x42 against 0x02; A Quiet Place Part II, also refused, carries 0x02 there like F1. Nothing in the first payload tracks the split
note: the tool itself is the result: these bytes could not be read before, and a byte scan for the sync word finds 45 candidates in a title that holds 603 blocks
